**Portugal vs. Spain, 2026 FIFA World Cup Round of 16, scheduled for July 6 at AT&T Stadium (also called Dallas Stadium) in Arlington, Texas (neutral venue).**[[1]](https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/yamal-vs-ronaldo-part-2-spain-portugal-meet-world-cup-round-16)[[2]](https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/spain-portugal-preview-live-stream-team-news-tickets)

This is the third World Cup meeting between the neighbors (following Spain’s 1-0 win in the 2010 Round of 16 and a 3-3 draw in the 2018 group stage). Spain holds the overall historical edge (roughly 18 wins to Portugal’s 7, with 16 draws across ~41-42 meetings), though results are closer in major tournaments.[[3]](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/spain-vs-portugal-history-european-021258469.html)[[4]](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/7/6/portugal-vs-spain-fifa-world-cup-last-16-ronaldo-yamal-prediction-kickoff-start-time)

Their most recent competitive clash was the 2025 UEFA Nations League final (2-2, Spain won on penalties).[[1]](https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/yamal-vs-ronaldo-part-2-spain-portugal-meet-world-cup-round-16)[[4]](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/7/6/portugal-vs-spain-fifa-world-cup-last-16-ronaldo-yamal-prediction-kickoff-start-time)

**Recent form (group stage, prior to the Round of 16):** Both sides advanced unbeaten. Spain delivered a dominant 3-0 win over Austria (with Mikel Oyarzabal among the scorers and in the Golden Boot conversation). Portugal edged Croatia 2-1. Spain entered the knockout stage with strong momentum after their first World Cup knockout win since 2010.[[1]](https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/yamal-vs-ronaldo-part-2-spain-portugal-meet-world-cup-round-16)[[5]](https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2026/07/02/spain-portugal-world-cup-prediction-analysis-odds/90790746007/)

**Injuries/suspensions:** Pre-match reports indicated no major concerns for Portugal. Spain faced a hamstring issue for Nico Williams (out); other doubts mentioned in some previews included Yeremi Pino and others, but the squad remained deep overall.[[4]](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/7/6/portugal-vs-spain-fifa-world-cup-last-16-ronaldo-yamal-prediction-kickoff-start-time)[[6]](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/portugal-vs-spain-world-cup-030000235.html)

**Travel/fatigue:** Both teams were based in North America for the group stage. Spain played in Los Angeles (their Round of 32 match), while Portugal played in Toronto—long cross-country or cross-border trips to Dallas for the knockout clash.[[1]](https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/yamal-vs-ronaldo-part-2-spain-portugal-meet-world-cup-round-16)

**Venue conditions:** AT&T Stadium is a domed indoor venue in Dallas/Arlington, Texas (low altitude, no significant elevation issues). The closed roof means a controlled environment with minimal weather impact on the pitch or play, though Texas summer heat could affect fans or pre/post-match activities. Standard professional pitch conditions expected.[[7]](https://www.facebook.com/fox6news/videos/world-cup-rowi-portugal-and-spain/1036661782393619/)

**Crowd/home advantage:** Neutral venue with an expected large, passionate attendance (historical figures around 70,000 cited in coverage). Significant support from Iberian diaspora and traveling fans for both sides, creating an electric derby atmosphere without a true home advantage.[[8]](https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2026/07/05/portugal-vs-spain-where-when-how-to-watch/90812165007/)

**Other notable storylines:** Cristiano Ronaldo (potentially in his final World Cup) vs. young Spanish star Lamine Yamal headlined the matchup, alongside the intense Iberian rivalry. Spain were generally viewed as slight favorites due to squad depth, recent form, and attacking quality, but Portugal’s talent and knockout experience made it a tight, high-stakes contest. Both teams emphasized the intensity beyond typical stakes.[[3]](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/spain-vs-portugal-history-european-021258469.html)[[4]](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/7/6/portugal-vs-spain-fifa-world-cup-last-16-ronaldo-yamal-prediction-kickoff-start-time)

All details above draw from pre-July 3, 2026 publications and historical records known before that date. Post-match or later information (including the actual result) has been disregarded per instructions.

factors.impact: Spain advanced with a dominant 3-0 win and strong momentum, achieving their first World Cup knockout win since 2010. Portugal 'edged' their opponent 2-1, indicating a less commanding performance in the group stage, which clearly favors Spain.

Spain holds a significant overall historical edge. While major tournament results are closer, Spain defeated Portugal in the 2010 World Cup and won their most recent competitive clash (2025 UEFA Nations League final on penalties), suggesting an ability to perform when it counts against their rivals.

Spain faces a notable setback with key attacker Nico Williams out due to a hamstring injury. Portugal, conversely, has no major injury concerns. This partially mitigates Spain's advantages and slightly favors Portugal.

Pre-match reports generally viewed Spain as 'slight favorites' due to their squad depth, recent form, and attacking quality, despite acknowledging Portugal's talent and knockout experience making it a tight affair.

analysis.reasoning: Spain enters this Round of 16 clash with a noticeable edge, driven primarily by their superior recent form and momentum from the group stage, highlighted by a dominant win. Their strong historical head-to-head record and recent competitive success against Portugal (including the 2025 Nations League final) reinforce their position. While the injury to Nico Williams is a significant blow for Spain, their squad depth is noted as strong, and the general pre-match consensus favored them. Portugal's less convincing group stage performance, despite their talent and experience, slightly diminishes their standing relative to Spain.
